sa_help_open_body_light: Open file/PDB at the top takes a structure file from this computer (PDB, mmCIF, SDF, MOL2, XYZ), or downloads an entry from the PDB by its ID. You can also drop a file anywhere on the page. On iPhone and iPad, a page opened directly from a file (from Mail or the Files app) may not be able to use the internet: if loading from the PDB fails, the app offers a link that downloads the entry in the browser; then open the downloaded file with Open file/PDB.
sa_help_open_body_full: Open file/PDB at the top takes a structure file from this computer (PDB, mmCIF, SDF, MOL2, XYZ, or a .pse session, which opens in "Includes PyMOL™" mode), or downloads an entry from the PDB by its ID. You can also drop a file anywhere on the page. On iPhone and iPad, a page opened directly from a file (from Mail or the Files app) may not be able to use the internet: if loading from the PDB fails, the app offers a link that downloads the entry in the browser; then open the downloaded file with Open file/PDB.
sa_help_move_body: With a mouse: drag with the left button to turn the structure, the right button to zoom and the middle button to move it. On a touch screen: one finger turns it, pinching zooms, two fingers move it. On a phone, View in the bottom bar also has zoom buttons. In "Includes PyMOL™" mode on a computer, 🖱 Mouse controls at the right end of its menu row lists every mouse action in words.
sa_help_engines_body_full: "3Dmol.js" mode is light and starts at once. "Includes PyMOL™" mode does much more (its menus and command line), but it is heavy: it takes a while to start and uses 0.5–1.5 GB of memory. Switch between them with the control at the top right (on a phone, Mode in the bottom bar).
sa_help_engines_body_light: This edition shows structures in "3Dmol.js" mode, which is light and starts at once. The full edition adds "Includes PyMOL™" mode.
sa_help_save_body: Save image (the camera button) saves a screenshot of the view, or a ray-traced picture made in "Includes PyMOL™" mode. Export saves the structure file, the 3D shapes and the files of "Includes PyMOL™" mode; Save as HTMLapp there makes a copy of this whole app, with the structure in it, to send to someone. Each file is made first, then saved to the browser's default location or, where the browser can, to a place you choose.
sa_help_offline_body: Viewing works offline: everything runs inside this one file, nothing is installed, and the files you open are sent nowhere. It connects to the internet only when you load an entry from the PDB (RCSB, files.rcsb.org), press Check the latest version on GitHub (api.github.com) or Save the latest version with the current data as a separate file (raw.githubusercontent.com), or open a link out of the file. On iPhone and iPad, a page opened directly from a file may not be able to connect at all, even when the browser can; viewing and opening files still work.

sa_chg_intro: "Includes PyMOL™" mode runs Open-Source PyMOL {{version}}, built from pymol-open-source commit {{commit}} and compiled to WebAssembly for Pyodide {{pyodide}} so that it runs inside the browser. It is a modified build made by AgroDesign Studios and distinct from the products of Schrödinger, LLC.
